hints: Find range of $fg$ on $x \ge 0$ as $y \ge 11 \implies$ Domain of $(fg)^{-1}$ is $x \ge 11$.
walkthrough:
Set $y = 2(3x + 2)^2 + 3$ and solve for $x$ on $x \ge 0$ (where $3x + 2 \ge 2 > 0$):
$$2(3x + 2)^2 = y - 3 \implies (3x + 2)^2 = \frac{y - 3}{2}$$
$$3x + 2 = \sqrt{\frac{y - 3}{2}} \implies 3x = \sqrt{\frac{y - 3}{2}} - 2 \implies x = \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{\frac{y - 3}{2}} - \frac{2}{3}$$
$$(fg)^{-1}(x) = \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{\frac{x - 3}{2}} - \frac{2}{3}$$

Determine the domain of $(fg)^{-1}$ from the range of $fg$ for $x \ge 0$:
$$x \ge 0 \implies fg(x) \ge 2(3(0) + 2)^2 + 3 = 2(4) + 3 = 11$$
$$\text{Domain of } (fg)^{-1}: \quad x \ge 11 \quad (\text{or } [11, \infty))$$

Equate $gf(2x) = fg(x)$ and solve for $x$:
$$24x^2 + 11 = 18x^2 + 24x + 11 \implies 6x^2 - 24x = 0$$
$$6x(x - 4) = 0 \implies x = 0 \quad \text{or} \quad x = 4$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } x = 0, \quad 4)$$
